subject: Private hosting discovery — pain points, scope & commitments
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Murray <alicia.murray@cardinalhealth.com>, Tom Chen <tom.chen@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Private hosting discovery — pain points, scope & commitments

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared
- PHI data residency and strict egress controls: staging/production data cannot leave on-prem or designated GovCloud region.
- Procurement and security teams require customer-managed key material (HSM/KMS) with attestable key usage and no persistent outbound connections.
- Current stack constraints: existing on-prem K8s cluster (RHEL nodes behind corporate proxy), HashiCorp Vault for secrets, and a constrained maintenance window (Sundays 02:00–06:00 local) for any air-gap syncs.
- Throughput: bursty inference up to ~120 TPS for short windows; typical steady-state 10–15 TPS.

Success criteria you called out
- Deployment in your VPC / on-prem footprint with KMS integration (customer HSM or CloudHSM).
- No data exfiltration outside allowed endpoints; support for explicit allowlisted egress and outbound proxy.
- SLA on latency percentiles for P99 <= 800ms for 512-token requests (or a documented fallback).
- Auditability: access logs, model versioning, and per-tenant tracing for compliance & audits.

Assumptions we made during the call
- You can provide an allowlist of egress IPs and a NAT or proxy configuration.
- You are open to a two-phase POC: (1) isolated on-prem pilot using a sandbox dataset; (2) staged production rollout with reserved capacity.

Deliverables Redwood will provide by EOD Wednesday (Aug 18)
1) Private hosting checklist (attached): network ports, proxies, certs, KMS integration checklist.
2) Proposed POC timeline and minimal infra BOM (attached).
3) Short list of questions for your security team (we'll share as a one-pager).

Open questions for you
- Confirm whether the Vault instance is reachable from a dedicated subnet or if we must use an edge-proxy approach.
- Who is the procurement POC and estimated procurement window (we heard ~8–10 weeks)?
- Which identity provider will be authoritative for operator access (Okta / Azure AD / on-prem LDAP)?

Next steps
- You: reply with procurement POC and preferred time for a 45-min technical deep-dive with Dev (solutions engineer) next week.
- Us: deliver the checklist + POC timeline by Wed, Aug 18 and sample network allowlist.

Attachments:
- redwood-private-checklist.pdf (3 pages)
- proposed-poc-timeline.xlsx

Thanks again — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,

Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Camila —

Thanks for the thorough summary, this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement POC is procurement@cardinalhealth.com (Sara Lee is the lead). Timeline: as long as the SOW and security packaging are standard, procurement estimates 6–9 weeks for a standard SaaS + on-prem integration. If we require an AMS amendment or custom NDA, add ~3 weeks.
- We will need SOC 2 Type II and penetration test evidence before production. Please include a link to the most recent reports (we can accept redacted).
- For KMS: we prefer using our on-prem HSM (Thales) with an HSM-to-CloudHSM bridge only if the key material never leaves our boundary. Need to see an integration pattern.
- Regarding maintenance: the Sunday 02:00–06:00 window is correct; any changes outside that window need pre-approval.

Tom (copied) — can you confirm the Vault reachability?

Alicia
Director, Applied Infrastructure — Cardinal Health
alicia.murray@cardinalhealth.com | +1 (202) 555-0118

Camila / Alicia —

Quick technical note: Vault is currently in a segmented management VPC with a peered connectivity to our on-prem gateway. There is no direct outbound internet egress from the Vault subnet; requests must go through our corporate proxy (Squid) which performs TLS interception.

We can provide a jump-host or a dedicated proxy endpoint for the Redwood agent to talk to Vault, but Vault will only accept mTLS-authenticated clients. We will also need an IDS-safe workflow for accepting binaries into the environment — i.e., no unvetted containers.

On the throughput numbers — the burst to 120 TPS aligns with a few high-load batch events (insurance claim reconciliation). If we do a POC, our preference is a sandbox dataset (de-identified) and a capacity cap so we don't affect production.

Happy to join the tech deep-dive. Alicia, Sara (procurement) — please propose 2x 45-min windows next week.

Thanks,
Tom
Lead Infra Architect — Cardinal Health

Grace / Dev — looping you both for the technical deep-dive planning and to confirm feasibility of the constraints above. Key asks for the session:

- Dev: please prepare a short runbook (3–4 slides) that outlines our recommended KMS/HSM integration patterns for on-prem Thales + Redwood (options: direct HSM integration via PKCS#11 shim, proxy-based envelope keys, or hybrid CloudHSM with hardware attestations).
- Dev: propose a minimal pilot topology that fits inside a locked sandbox (non-prod K8s namespace, 2 x g4dn-equivalent for inference, separate logging pipeline). Include estimated vCPU/GPU, RAM, and expected P99 numbers.
- Grace: rough commercial posture for a 3-month POC (reserved capacity pricing + estimated infra adders).
- Myself: I'll share the checklist and the proposed POC timeline (attached earlier) with Alicia and Sara.

Please advise if any of this is a hard no; otherwise, can we target Wed Aug 25 or Thu Aug 26 for the 45-min technical deep-dive? Alicia / Tom / Sara — are either of those days workable?

Thanks,
Camila
